topic: Why The Spinning Top Was Never Dom Cobb's Real Totem
core_thesis: The spinning top belonged to Mal. Dom Cobb's real totem is his golden wedding ring, which only appears on his finger when he is dreaming.
canonical_facts: A totem's fundamental rule is that only the owner can know its exact weight and balance (Arthur explicitly states this to Ariadne).
Cobb tells Ariadne that the spinning top was Mal's totem, violating the single rule of totems.
In every scene set in the real world (e.g. Mombasa chase, Paris meeting, final airport arrival), Cobb does not wear a wedding ring.
In every scene set inside a dream layer (e.g. Saito's palace, the hotel, the fortress, limbo), Cobb wears a thick gold wedding band on his left hand.
interpretations: Audiences obsess over whether the top falls in the final shot, but the final shot deliberately cuts before showing Cobb's bare left hand as he embraces his children.

verified_claims.source: Christopher Nolan Film Analysis & Frame Inspection

scene_evidence.detail: Cobb's left hand visible while climbing wall, no ring.
Cobb holds gun, thick gold band clearly visible on left ring finger.
